status: v10 Apple-inspired proposal for Backleaf: white/black content surfaces, gray chrome only, blue folder identity and selection emphasis; hierarchy by restrained elevation, never by outlines or full-surface color blocks

rules.apple_semantics: The main content canvas stays white (light) or true black (dark). Gray is reserved for chrome, sidebars, grouped sections and separators, not for the main content surface or folder identity.
rules.hierarchy: Hierarchy and focus are expressed with restrained elevation (floating identity surface, floating panels, soft shadow) instead of outlines or full-surface color fills.
rules.normal: Flat content layer; folder identity keeps its blue artwork; file-type artworks keep their own category colors.
rules.hover: Lift only the hovered identity/row by one level; no fill change, no stroke, no text color change.
rules.pressed: Reduce the shadow and move down 1px; no new color surface.
rules.selected: Raised identity surface (radius 10) plus blue filename; no blue/gray fill behind the whole cell. Selection emphasis lives in elevation and the filename tint.
rules.focus: Soft accent halo around the identity; accessibility indicator only, never a thick outline.
rules.inactive-selected: Keep the raised geometry; reduce shadow strength; filename returns to primary content color.
rules.disabled: Lower opacity only; no new outline or color block.
rules.floating: Menus, task panels and dialogs use floating surfaces plus layered soft shadows; content remains white/black rather than gray.
rules.file-types: Word/PDF/Excel/code/archive etc. keep their existing category colors; a theme change must never recolor file-type art.
rules.match-highlight: Search matches use a dedicated warm amber highlight distinct from blue selection; the highlight carries its own readable content color.
